Why You'll Love This how to cook jasmine rice

  • It makes tender, fragrant rice with a fluffy texture.
  • The simple stovetop method uses everyday ingredients.
  • Rinsing the rice helps remove excess starch for better grains.
  • It is ready in about 30 minutes, including resting time.
  • This versatile side pairs beautifully with curries, vegetables, beans, and more.

Ingredients

Gather these simple kitchen staples for a comforting pot of jasmine rice that is ready to round out just about any meal.

  • Jasmine rice - 2 cups
  • Water - 2 1/2 cups
  • Salt - 1/2 teaspoon
  • Neutral cooking oil - 1 teaspoon

How to Make How to Cook Jasmine Rice

Plan for 5 minutes of prep and 25 minutes of cooking time. The rice cooks for 15 minutes, then rests covered for 10 minutes so the grains can finish steaming gently.

Step 1: Measure the Rice

Measure the jasmine rice into a fine-mesh strainer. A fine mesh keeps the small grains from slipping through.

Step 2: Rinse the Rice

Rinse the rice under cool running water until the water runs mostly clear. This removes extra surface starch and helps the cooked rice turn out fluffy.

Step 3: Drain Thoroughly

Let the rice drain thoroughly in the strainer. A good drain keeps extra water from changing the rice-to-water balance.

Step 4: Add the Ingredients

Add the drained rice, water, salt, and neutral cooking oil to a medium saucepan. Choose a saucepan with enough room for the rice to expand as it cooks.

Step 5: Stir Once

Stir the ingredients once to combine them. After this quick stir, the rice is ready to heat.

Step 6: Bring to a Gentle Boil

Bring the mixture to a gentle boil over medium-high heat. Watch the pan closely so the water does not boil over.

Step 7: Cover the Pan

Cover the saucepan with a tight-fitting lid. A snug lid helps hold in the steam that cooks the rice evenly.

Step 8: Lower the Heat

Reduce the heat to low as soon as the pan is covered. The gentle heat keeps the rice from scorching on the bottom.

Step 9: Cook the Rice

Cook the rice for 15 minutes without lifting the lid. Keeping the lid closed preserves the steam needed for tender grains.

Step 10: Remove from Heat

Remove the saucepan from the heat after the 15-minute cooking time. Keep the lid in place so the trapped steam can continue working.

Step 11: Let the Rice Rest

Let the covered rice rest for 10 minutes. This short resting time helps the moisture settle throughout the pot.

Step 12: Fluff and Serve

Fluff the rice gently with a fork before serving. Lift and separate the grains rather than stirring vigorously, which can make them sticky.

Pro Tips for Making how to cook jasmine rice

  • Rinse until the water is mostly clear, but do not worry if it is not perfectly transparent.
  • Drain the rice well before adding it to the saucepan for the most reliable texture.
  • Use a tight-fitting lid and resist checking the rice while it cooks.
  • Let the rice rest covered for the full 10 minutes before fluffing.
  • Use a fork to fluff gently so the cooked grains stay light and separate.

How to Serve this how to cook jasmine rice

  • Spoon it alongside a fragrant vegetable curry or bean stew.
  • Serve it with steamed vegetables and a favorite sauce for a simple supper.
  • Pair it with roasted chicken, baked fish, or tofu.
  • Add fresh herbs, sliced green onions, or a squeeze of lime just before serving.
  • Use leftovers as the base for a quick rice bowl with vegetables and beans.

Make Ahead and Storage

Storing Leftovers

  • Cool leftover rice promptly and refrigerate it in a covered container within 2 hours of cooking.
  • Store it in the refrigerator for up to 3 to 4 days.
  • Keep the rice in a shallow container when possible so it cools more evenly.

Freezing

  • Freeze cooled rice in airtight, freezer-safe containers or portioned bags.
  • Use frozen rice within 1 month for the best texture.
  • Thaw it in the refrigerator or reheat it directly from frozen.

Reheating

  • Reheat rice until it is steaming hot throughout.
  • Add a small splash of water before reheating to restore moisture.
  • Stir gently after reheating and serve right away.

Final Thoughts

Once you know how to cook jasmine rice this way, a warm and fluffy side is always close at hand for simple family suppers.

FAQs

Here are a few helpful answers for making this dependable jasmine rice recipe in your own kitchen.

Should I rinse jasmine rice before cooking?

Yes. Rinsing removes excess surface starch and helps the cooked grains turn out lighter and less sticky.

Can I skip the oil?

Yes, you can leave out the oil if you prefer. It adds a little richness and can help keep the grains from sticking.

Why should I keep the lid closed while the rice cooks?

The lid holds in the steam that cooks the rice. Lifting it can let out heat and moisture, which may leave the grains undercooked.

How do I know when jasmine rice is done?

After 15 minutes of low cooking and 10 minutes of covered resting, the water should be absorbed and the grains should be tender. Fluff gently with a fork before serving.
